title: Edge-AI chip efficiency vs model-accuracy tradeoff
bottleneck: Edge devices need milliwatt inference, but aggressive quantization, pruning, and tiny models sacrifice the accuracy and generality of frontier models. On-device learning is nearly absent, so edge models go stale, and heterogeneous edge SoCs lack the memory bandwidth for emerging workloads like on-device agents. The efficiency-accuracy Pareto frontier improves slowly.
why_it_blocks: If edge AI can't run capable models efficiently, intelligence stays cloud-tethered, with latency, privacy, and connectivity costs that block applications from robotics to rural healthcare. The edge remains a second-class citizen of the AI era.
current_state: NPUs in phones and MCUs now run impressive quantized models, and techniques like speculative decoding help. But the gap between edge-capable and frontier models keeps widening. On-device training is essentially absent, so edge models go stale while cloud models keep improving, widening the capability gap.
